screening_notes.disposition: NO SCORE MOVEMENT FOR ANY OF THE THREE
screening_notes.reasoning: The 19 September 2026 N.D. Cal. antitrust suit is a procedural event, not a conduct finding: nothing has been decided and no defendant has responded publicly. More importantly, the conduct the plaintiffs challenge is a public AI-safety commitment. The benchmark measures whether an institution recognises, responds to and reduces suffering; a claim that promising to slow down for safety reduced subscriber value does not map onto any of the 40 behavioural anchors as a harm. Scoring it negative would penalise a safety commitment. Scoring it positive would credit a lab on the strength of someone else complaining about it. Neither is defensible, so the correct output is a recorded screening note. Anthropic and OpenAI were confirmed on other evidence; xAI holds its floor. The countervailing 12 September Amodei pacing essay is logged as a positive watch item for Anthropic but is a commitment without a track record and is not banked as score.

A ransomware group posted a claim of a 1.22-terabyte AECOM breach on 17 September 2026 and plaintiffs' attorneys are investigating whether a class action can be filed. AECOM has neither confirmed nor denied it and no independent forensic source exists. A criminal group's self-serving claim is tier 1 and is not conduct evidence about the victim. It scored nothing in any dimension. AECOM was still given a first-ever evidence baseline from the public record, which confirmed at 47.5 vs 48.4.

LAHSA is a joint powers authority created by the City and County of Los Angeles, not a city department. Everyone charged on 16 September 2026 is a nonprofit contractor or contractor employee, not a City of Los Angeles official. The enforcing parties are the FBI and the United States Attorney, whose conduct is federal. Contractor crime and federal prosecution are not the scored entity's conduct. The existing 2026-09-14 LAHSA watch is advanced and sharpened, not satisfied.

The Florida Attorney General suit of 9 September 2026 was fully scored across all 40 subdimensions on 2026-09-15, which placed B5 and AB1 at the lower anchor-3 value precisely because of it. The scanner's evidence_date (2026-09-09) pre-dates that assessment and no later development was found. Re-scoring would count one event twice.

The 2026-09-14 Jamaica assessment examined Hurricane Melissa housing recovery only and did not look at policing at all. Tonight's evidence is therefore newly measured rather than newly occurring, which is legitimate because it is the state's own conduct documented by its own statutory oversight commission within the lookback window. EMP falls from 2.4 to 2.0 and INT from 2.4 to 2.2 on that evidence, offset by holding ACC at 2.4 because INDECOM's independent publication of unflattering fatality data is genuine accountability infrastructure (AB3 scored 4/5). Net delta -2.5, below the filing threshold, band unchanged.
